stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
Let $(X, \mathcal{O}_X)$ be a ringed space.
Set $R = \Gamma(X, \mathcal{O}_X)$. The category of
$\mathcal{O}_X$-modules which are summands of finite free
$\mathcal{O}_X$-modules is equivalent to the category of
finite projective $R$-modules.
hypotheses: $(X,\mathcal O_X)$ is a ringed space; put $R=\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$.
conclusions: The category of $\mathcal O_X$-modules that are direct summands of finite free $\mathcal O_X$-modules is equivalent to the category of finite projective $R$-modules.

reason: Reduces finite projective modules to finite free summands and applies the standard global-section/quasi-coherent sheaf equivalence.

stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
Let $(X, \mathcal{O}_X)$ be a ringed space. Let $M$ be an object
of $D(\mathcal{O}_X)$. The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $M$ is invertible in $D(\mathcal{O}_X)$, see
Categories, Definition \ref{categories-definition-invertible}, and
\item there is a locally finite direct product decomposition
$$
\mathcal{O}_X = \prod\nolimits_{n \in \mathbf{Z}} \mathcal{O}_n
$$
and for each $n$ there is an invertible $\mathcal{O}_n$-module
$\mathcal{H}^n$ (Modules, Definition \ref{modules-definition-invertible})
and $M = \bigoplus \mathcal{H}^n[-n]$ in $D(\mathcal{O}_X)$.
\end{enumerate}
If (1) and (2) hold, then $M$ is a perfect object of $D(\mathcal{O}_X)$. If
$\mathcal{O}_{X, x}$ is a local ring for all $x \in X$ these condition
are also equivalent to
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(3)] there exists an open covering $X = \bigcup U_i$
and for each $i$ an integer $n_i$ such that $M|_{U_i}$
is represented by an invertible $\mathcal{O}_{U_i}$-module
placed in degree $n_i$.
\end{enumerate}
hypotheses: $(X,\mathcal O_X)$ is any ringed space; $M\in D(\mathcal O_X)$.
For the additional equivalence with (3), assume all stalks $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ are local rings.
conclusions: Condition (1), that $M$ is tensor-invertible in $D(\mathcal O_X)$, is equivalent to (2), a locally finite product decomposition $\mathcal O_X=\prod_{n\in\mathbf Z}\mathcal O_n$ with invertible $\mathcal O_n$-modules $\mathcal H^n$ and $M\simeq\bigoplus_n\mathcal H^n[-n]$.
Under (1)–(2), $M$ is perfect. If all stalks are local, (3), that $M$ is locally an invertible module concentrated in a single (locally varying) degree, is also equivalent.

reason: Lengthy local equivalence proof includes a likely composition-order typo: b∘a−1=dh+hd where the homotopy is on the tensor complex and should involve a∘b; also omits a stalkwise equivalence direction.
